lines.name: BART Silicon Valley Phase II
lines.summary: VTA's six-mile extension of BART from Berryessa through downtown San José to Santa Clara, with three underground stations, one at-grade station and a rail yard, built around a single tunnel about 53 feet across. Its adopted budget is $12.7 billion. Early works are under way at the tunnel launch site, but the federal grant that would pay for about 40% of it is not yet signed, and service is scheduled for 2039 (VTA aims for 2037).

links.label: Project record in the megaprojects map

sources.note: Early construction ahead of tunneling: the West Portal launch structure excavated by September 2026; service "scheduled for 2039 (VTA aims for 2037)".
Early works: "crews have placed 75,000 cubic yards of concrete" (September 1, 2026).
"Q1-2039 RSD while managing to the aforementioned target RSD of Q2-2037"; the federal grant agreement proposed for Q4 2027.

lines.notes: Status as BAM's record of Oct 7, 2026 found it in the agencies' own documents. Checked again Oct 16, 2026 by web search on the agencies' own domains, which found nothing that changes it (their sites can't be reached from the build container; docs/research/future-status-2026-10.md). Early works for the tunnel are under way; the federal grant agreement is targeted for late 2027, and VTA is rebaselining the cost and schedule, which may move both dates.

lines.name: The Portal (Downtown Rail Extension)
lines.summary: A rail tunnel to bring Caltrain, and later high-speed rail, from the Fourth and King terminus about 1.3 miles into the Salesforce Transit Center, whose two-level underground train box was built for it and has stood empty since 2018. It adds an underground station at Fourth and Townsend. The $8.3 billion project is environmentally cleared and in federal engineering review, with a $3.38 billion federal grant in sight. It still needs the rest of its local and state funding, and TJPA forecasts service in late 2036.

sources.note: In FTA's Engineering phase since May 2024, not under construction or fully funded; "the Sept 2026 status report forecasts ready-for-service on Nov 17, 2036".

lines.name: California High-Speed Rail: San Francisco to San Jose
lines.summary: The Bay Area end of California's high-speed rail line. Rather than building new tracks up the Peninsula, high-speed trains would share Caltrain's newly electrified corridor for about 49 miles from San Francisco to San Jose, stopping at Fourth and King (and later the Salesforce Transit Center via The Portal), Millbrae for SFO, and San Jose Diridon. The route was environmentally approved in 2022, but no construction has started and the Authority's current plan reaches the Bay Area by 2039.

links.label: Project record in the megaprojects map

sources.note: Environmentally cleared (August 2022); right-of-way, design and station work not started, in a San Francisco–Bakersfield timeline that runs to 2039.
"fully approved and eligible for advanced design": the San Francisco to San José EIR/EIS certified in August 2022.

Adopted June 1, 2026. Bay Area service comes only in the San Francisco–Bakersfield scenario ("deliver SF-B by 2039"), which needs a state solution for San José to Gilroy; no opening is given for this section.
October 2026: a new environmental review of Gilroy to the Central Valley Wye, the link that would bring trains to San José, with new alignments to be decided by the end of 2027.

lines.name: Valley Link
lines.summary: A new passenger rail line along the I-580 corridor linking BART at Dublin/Pleasanton with ACE commuter trains at Vasco Road in Livermore, so riders from the San Joaquin Valley can change trains across a platform instead of driving over the Altamont Pass. The first 11 miles, with three stations and battery-electric trains, are environmentally cleared and in design; an extension to Mountain House is cleared but unfunded.

sources.note: Cleared and in design, construction funding not secured; "The schedule in the June 2026 MTC request shows construction from summer 2029 to opening in summer 2033."
"preparing to enter the engineering phase of the federal CIG program"; phased construction approved June 2025.

lines.name: SMART Healdsburg extension
lines.summary: The next step north for SMART's trains: about nine miles of railroad, idle for decades, rebuilt from today's end of the line at Windsor through Healdsburg, with a new Healdsburg station, a replacement Russian River rail bridge and the SMART Pathway alongside. It is funded at about $269 million, in design, and planned to open in late 2028; where the Healdsburg station goes is being reconsidered.

links.label: Project record in the megaprojects map

sources.note: Funded, cleared and in design; the first construction package due for award in October 2026, construction from spring 2027, service planned for December 2028.
"Design: September 2025 - December 2026; Construction: January 2027 - November 2028; Testing: November - December 2028; Service Begins: December 2028." $269 million secured.
Phase I (design) of the design-build contract under way; utility and roadway design agreements.
The station's location reopened for public engagement through November 2026 (Depot/Hudson Street or downtown).

Funded and cleared, in design; SMART's schedule starts construction in January 2027. Utility potholing since April 2026 informs the design. The California Transportation Commission was to consider a $162.2 million construction allocation on Oct 15-16, 2026. The Healdsburg station's site is under review again, so its point may move.

lines.name: SMART Cloverdale extension
lines.summary: The last leg of the voter-approved SMART system: about 13.5 miles of out-of-service railroad from north of Healdsburg to Cloverdale, with new stations at Geyserville (adopted in August 2026) and Cloverdale. It was environmentally cleared with the rest of the line and is in the regional plan, but it has no construction funding yet.

links.label: Project record in the megaprojects map

sources.note: Environmentally cleared with the 70-mile system, in Plan Bay Area 2050+, with no construction funding or schedule.
The extension is split into two nine-mile projects to compete for grants; a Geyserville station near Highway 128 and Remmel Road.
Geyserville station: statutory exemption from CEQA, August 20, 2026.
"Resolution 2026-26 adopts the Geyserville Station Project into SMART's program".
A state grant request for some components only; no construction funding committed. Awards pending in October 2026.
